title: Transition Timer
pin_title: ADHD Transition Timer: Set a Two-Minute Bridge Before Switching Tasks
description: Switching from one thing to another costs extra energy with ADHD. Before you stop the current task, set a two-minute timer and name the next tiny action out loud. The timer is a bridge, not a deadline. When it rings you already know the first step of the next thing, so the gap feels smaller. Two minutes is short enough that it does not feel like another chore. #ADHD #Transitions #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Park the Thought
pin_title: ADHD Park the Thought: Write the Idea Down and Come Back Later
description: A useful idea that arrives while you are busy can pull you off track. Write the idea on a sticky note or in a notes app and leave it there. Tell yourself you will look at it after the current thing. The note keeps the idea safe so your brain does not have to hold it. You can return when the timer ends or the task is done. #ADHD #Focus #ADHDTips #Ideas

title: One Song Start
pin_title: ADHD One Song Start: Play a Song and Begin During the First Verse
description: Waiting to feel ready can last all day. Pick one song you like and press play. Your only job is to start the task while the first verse is playing. When the song ends you can stop or keep going. The music gives a soft boundary and makes the beginning feel lighter. Most days you will still be working when the song finishes. #ADHD #Starting #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Standing Stretch
pin_title: ADHD Standing Stretch: Stand Up for Thirty Seconds Between Tasks
description: Sitting too long makes the next start feel heavier. When you finish one thing, stand up and stretch your arms for thirty seconds before you sit again. The movement resets your body and gives your brain a tiny break. You do not need a full walk. Thirty seconds of standing is enough to loosen the stiffness and make the next task feel more possible. #ADHD #Movement #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Label the Drawer
pin_title: ADHD Label the Drawer: Put a Clear Word on the Outside So You Find Things
description: When you cannot see what is inside, every drawer becomes a small search. Write one word on a piece of tape and stick it on the front: cables, pens, snacks. The label removes the guesswork. Next time you need the item you already know which drawer to open. Clear labels turn memory into something you can see. #ADHD #Organization #ADHDTips #FindThings

title: Water Bottle Note
pin_title: ADHD Water Bottle Note: Stick a Tiny Reminder on the Bottle Itself
description: You can forget to drink even when the bottle is on the desk. Stick a small piece of tape on the bottle with the word sip or a smiley face. Every time you notice the note you take a drink. The reminder travels with the bottle so you do not need an extra app or alarm. One word is enough. #ADHD #Hydration #ADHDTips #Habits

title: Doorway Pause
pin_title: ADHD Doorway Pause: Stop for Five Seconds Before You Leave the Room
description: Walking out of a room and then realizing you forgot something is common. Pause in the doorway for five seconds and glance back. Ask yourself if you have the one thing you came for. The short stop catches the missing item before you walk away. Five seconds is faster than going back later. #ADHD #Forgetfulness #ADHDTips #Leaving

title: Evening Lights Dim
pin_title: ADHD Evening Lights: Dim the Room Lights So Your Body Knows Night Is Coming
description: Bright overhead lights can keep your brain in daytime mode. Turn the main lights down or switch to a lamp an hour before bed. The softer light is a signal that the day is ending. Your body starts to settle without a strict bedtime rule. Dim light is a gentle boundary that does not feel like a punishment. #ADHD #EveningRoutine #Sleep #ADHDTips
